blocks.title: Real time on the real map
blocks.text: Satellite imagery, {provinces} provinces and great-circle routes: an air raid takes as long as the real flight, a fleet sails around continents. The game goes on even while you are offline.

blocks.title: Real arsenals and budgets
blocks.text: Every nation starts with its estimated 2025 order of battle and its defense budget in US dollars. {systems} real weapon systems, from the F-35 to the Leclerc tank, with their unit price.

blocks.title: Intelligence and fog of war
blocks.text: You only see what your sensors detect. Spies, sources, satellites and radars lift the veil; sabotage and technology theft weaken your opponents.

blocks.title: Diplomacy and the Security Council
blocks.text: Alliances, agreements, production licences and Security Council votes with veto power. War is declared by the first attack — or the first border crossed.

blocks.title: Single-player or up to {players} players
blocks.text: Play alone against more than two hundred AI nations or join a persistent game where unclaimed nations stay under AI control. Seasonal rankings.

howto.title: How to play Red Line — beginner's guide
howto.description: Guide to Red Line, the real-time geopolitical strategy game: pick a nation, move your armies, produce, research, spy, negotiate and win.
howto.lead: Red Line is played in real time: your orders are carried out while the world keeps moving. Here is what you need for your first hours in command.

sections.title: 1. Start a game
paragraphs: Click **Play for free**: a single-player game starts right away with a guest account, no sign-up needed. Create an account to find your games on any device and to join multiplayer.
Choose a scenario, then a nation. Every nation is playable; great powers have more means, small nations offer a tougher challenge.

sections.title: 2. Read the map
paragraphs: The map is the real world map, in satellite imagery, divided into {provinces} provinces. Your territory is shown in purple. Markers show detected units: precise near your sensors, approximate further away.
Game time flows continuously, at the speed chosen when the game was created. A clock shows the in-game day and time.
list: Select a unit, then a destination: the route follows the great circle and avoids impassable land.
An attack order or entering a foreign province automatically declares war.
Combat is resolved in regular rounds; range, detection, armour and stealth matter — terrain does not.

sections.title: 3. Produce and research
paragraphs: Your defense budget pays for production, upkeep and research. Every system has a real unit price, a build time and technology prerequisites: no fifth-generation fighter without the matching R&D.
Production licences let you build foreign equipment; the black market can help, at the risk of being exposed.

sections.title: 4. Intelligence
paragraphs: Three services — internal security, foreign intelligence, military intelligence — receive a budget and run operations: plant a spy, recruit a source, turn an agent, steal technology, sabotage a factory. A daily report sums up what you have learned.

sections.title: 5. Diplomacy and the Security Council
paragraphs: Propose alliances and agreements, buy licences, manage your internal stability. Every 30 in-game days the Security Council meets: permanent members with veto power and rotating seats vote on resolutions.

sections.title: 6. Win
paragraphs: Victory is military only: control 60% of the world's provinces or every enemy capital. A single-player game with no login for 48 hours is closed as abandoned (24 hours without any player in multiplayer).

tips: Protect your capital: taking every enemy capital is one of the two victory conditions.
Air defense and radars pay off: a downed fighter is worth tens of millions of dollars.
Don't declare war on everyone at once: a well-chosen alliance is worth an armoured division.
Check in regularly: the game goes on without you, and long orders run while you are away.

features.title: Red Line features — real-time military strategy
features.description: Real world map, {nations} nations, {systems} real military systems, defense budgets in US dollars, intelligence, diplomacy, Security Council, multiplayer with up to {players} players.
features.lead: Red Line is an online war game built around realistic means and clear command: a clean tactical console laid over the real world map.

items.title: The real world map
items.text: NASA satellite imagery (Blue Marble), current borders and {provinces} provinces with their cities. Movement follows great circles, fleets sail around continents, straits matter.
points: Navigation on a global hexagonal grid
Zoom from the globe down to cities

items.title: Real arsenals, real dollars
items.text: Every nation starts with its estimated order of battle and its real defense budget. The {systems} systems of the catalogue have their real characteristics and unit price; a real photograph illustrates each entry.
points: Ships, submarines, missiles, satellites, nuclear deterrence

items.title: Production gated by R&D
items.text: A technology tree governs production: aircraft generations, stealth, armed drones, missile defense. Production licences and the black market open other paths.
points: General mobilisation, at the economy's expense

items.title: Intelligence and fog of war
items.text: You only see what your radars, satellites and agents detect. The server never sends your browser what your nation does not know: reading network traffic gives no edge.

items.title: Diplomacy and the Security Council
items.text: Alliances, agreements and votes: the Security Council meets every 30 in-game days, with permanent members, veto power and rotating seats. Internal stability can lead to revolt or a coup.

items.title: Single-player and multiplayer
items.text: Alone against more than two hundred AI nations, or in a persistent game with up to {players} players: the game goes on while you are away and an AI holds your nation if you go inactive. Seasonal rankings, spectators, border timelapse.

items.title: Terminal interface, on every screen
items.text: A modern, dense and readable command interface, designed for desktop and mobile alike. Nothing to download: the game runs in your browser.

items.title: Fair by design
items.text: Free to play. Premium currency speeds things up or personalises, with no random purchases (no loot boxes); competitive games limit or disable in-game purchases.

faq.title: Red Line FAQ — frequently asked questions
faq.description: Answers to frequently asked questions about Red Line: price, multiplayer, mobile, realism of the armies, game length, purchases, personal data.
faq.lead: Everything you need to know before taking command.

items.a: Yes. The game is free and runs in your browser, with nothing to download. An optional premium currency speeds up some actions or buys cosmetics; no purchase is random.
No: “Play for free” opens a guest account kept on your device. A registered account (email and password) lets you find your games anywhere, play multiplayer and appear in the rankings.
Yes. The interface is designed for desktop, tablet and phone. The game can also be installed as an app from your browser.
Up to {players} human players in multiplayer; the other nations are controlled by the AI. In single-player you face more than two hundred AI nations.

items.q: How long does a game last?
items.a: A game is played in real time over several days or weeks, at the speed chosen when it was created. It goes on while you are offline: a few check-ins a day are enough.

items.q: Are the armies and budgets real?
items.a: They are based on public estimates: 2025 defense budgets in US dollars, estimated orders of battle and {systems} real systems with their unit price. The game remains fiction: no real-world target is depicted, strategic objectives are generic.
Militarily only: by controlling 60% of the world's provinces or every enemy capital.

items.q: Is Red Line an alternative to Conflict of Nations?
items.a: Red Line is inspired by it: the same global scale and real-time play, plus real arsenals and budgets, detailed intelligence, a Security Council and a clean command interface with no random purchases.
Cosmetics have no military effect. Speed-ups are governed by each game: open, capped or disabled for competitive games.

items.q: Which languages is the game available in?
items.a: French and English, with more languages coming progressively.
Only what the game needs: account, games, technical security logs. No advertising trackers. Details are in the [privacy policy](page:legal:privacy).

items.q: How old do I need to be?
items.a: At least 15, or with the consent of a parent or guardian. The game depicts armed conflict strategically, without graphic violence.
